# Route projects by complexity

Separate routine execution, complex coordination and material decisions.

## Working categories

| Category       | Practical characteristics                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Standard       | Established workflow, ordinary documentation and clear funding/payout route.                |
| Complex        | Specific funder obligations, several parties, tailored reporting or a nonstandard workflow. |
| Strategic fund | Programme-wide coordination, significant governance implications or complex regranting.     |

The earlier matrix used monetary bands. Do not use those bands alone to approve a project or establish signing authority. A project can be strategically or legally complex at any amount.

## Routing record

Record the category, reason, case owner, execution responsibilities and next action. Laura reviews every incoming application first, then assigns it to herself or Ivan, or refers the appropriate misdirected open-source application to Lucas for OSE.

## A genuine exception

Identify the actual departure from the applicable arrangement. A host redirection, incomplete file or high amount alone is not enough. Define the affected commitment and obtain the required decision before relying on an exception.

Use the [lightweight exception register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/10XFG2WgtWxz-c9X0kbn-sA2OPhSWVOrEGbI_m1x5z9M/edit) as the workstream reference. The [plan reviewed on 22 September 2026](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ghToLzMnkuzCyowZi0sh6aBz3jMc5RPU1uU-AOBT3Qs/edit) marks J1-05 complete and records documented use. Continue to track conditions and review dates in that register; completion of the tool does not close individual cases or authorise a new deviation. The archived broad checklist is historical.

## Reassess when facts change

If the beneficiary, legal arrangement, funding or payment route changes, review the classification and authority again. A previous classification is not permanent approval for expanded activity.

# Administer the Global Statelessness Fund

Coordinate programme delivery while retaining a defensible payment and reporting trail.

GSF is documented as an internal OCEF fund supporting work on statelessness and nationality rights. Its mission includes reaching informal or otherwise difficult-to-fund groups. Platform labels may not fully represent this internal-fund arrangement.

#### Operational roles

Laura coordinates fund delivery and programme follow-up; Ivan executes the documented payment and platform work; CFO provides financial control; JF handles material executive decisions. Programme leadership retains its programme role under the actual governance arrangement.

#### Grant cycle

1. Identify the approved activity, recipient, purpose and programme decision.
2. Confirm the agreement and payment route, including any distinction between grantee and payee.
3. Collect proportionate evidence that meets the actual banking, financial and contractual requirements.
4. Obtain the required review and execute through [payment processing](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/payment-processing-and-disbursements).
5. Record payment, allocation, reporting date and next action in the existing grant record.
6. Retain reporting and closure evidence.

#### Sensitive circumstances

The fund’s accessible approach does not remove the need for a defensible record. Explain the purpose of requested information and seek an approved alternative where the standard document or route creates a real obstacle. Do not reproduce individual cases in this handbook.

#### Internal expenses and cards

Keep GSF’s internal operational activity distinguishable from onward grants and other hosted collectives. Card transactions need receipts and manual records where the workflow requires them; see [internal virtual cards](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/virtual-cards).

#### Currency and reporting

The existing records describe USD and EUR activity and manual reporting limitations. Verify entity, fund, currency and report scope before allocation or reporting. Do not use a second profile as an unexplained substitute for the financial record.

Laura should confirm the current grant register and restricted Grantees folder with the programme team; keep links in the operational record rather than inventing a new tracker.

#### Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. Consolidated audit D10 and the existing GSF/role documentation. Financial treatment and the applicable delegation still follow their dedicated validation routes.

Sensitive evidence belongs with the transaction or restricted financial record, not in a reusable procedure.

# Accounting tools and working arrangements

This note explains how OCEF's accounting information is assembled and how the main tools fit together. It complements the [quarterly accounting procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting) and the [finance cycle](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/financial-ops-task-overview).

## Tools and records

| Tool                      | Use in the accounting workflow                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **WinBooks**              | Bookkeeping software used by Saïd at Comfisgest. The accounting ledger, journals and balances are maintained here.                                                                          |
| **Virtual Invoice**       | Supporting invoice processing alongside WinBooks, using PDF and XML documents.                                                                                                              |
| **Billit / Peppol**       | Collection of electronic invoices. Invoices received outside this channel also need to be included in the accounting pack.                                                                  |
| **Google Drive**          | Working folders for invoices, bank statements, payroll documents, platform exports and accounting preparation files.                                                                        |
| **Open Collective**       | Operational transaction and allocation records, including EUR/USD exports and administrative contribution data. These records are reconciled with bank movements and the accounting ledger. |
| **Google Sheets / Excel** | Preparation and review of exports, revenue schedules and reconciliation working files.                                                                                                      |
| **SD Worx / eDox**        | Payroll accounting documents and the payroll provider's invoices; both are needed.                                                                                                          |

Confirm the working WinBooks file and access arrangements with Saïd before making entries or relying on an export. A local copy, a shared environment and a downloaded report should not be assumed to contain identical data.

## Coordination

[Saïd](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/accountant-said) handles bookkeeping, accounts and returns within the scope of his engagement. The [CFO](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/cfo-budget-and-financial-control) coordinates accounting requests, instructions and financial review. Ivan owns accounting document collection and preparation, including OCEF operating expenses, and follows VAT filing and payment through to the supporting confirmations, with CFO review. Laura provides project and funding information where needed. See the [quarterly accounting procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting#responsibility-and-vat-follow-up) for the detailed steps and authority boundaries.

The detailed allocation of invoice entry, bank entry, review, filing and payment must be clear for each accounting cycle. Access to a tool does not itself assign responsibility or payment authority. Refer to the [operational RACI](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle) for responsibilities.

## Quarterly accounting and VAT preparation

The working cycle includes a quarterly collection of documents for accounting and VAT preparation:

* Purchase invoices from Billit in PDF and XML, plus invoices received elsewhere.
* SD Worx invoices and payroll accounting documents.
* Statements for all relevant bank and payment accounts, separated by entity and currency.
* Open Collective exports for the same period.
* Schedules supporting hosting fees and grant-related administrative contributions.
* Explanations and supporting documents for allocations, transfers and unresolved differences.

Follow [Prepare quarterly accounting records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting) for filing and review. Confirm the collection deadline, applicable filing deadline and payment instructions with the accountant for each period. Preparing a return, filing it and paying the amount due are separate steps.

## Reconciliation and completion records

Bank statements, Open Collective records and the accounting ledger serve different purposes. Use the [reconciliation procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/reconciliation-process) to connect them, keeping currencies, internal transfers, fees and project allocations distinguishable.

For each period, retain the reviewed accounting pack, unresolved-item list, relevant filing acknowledgements and payment confirmations in the restricted accounting records. For annual accounts, also retain the approved version and evidence of the applicable approval and filing steps.

This note describes the working setup; it does not certify that a particular period is reconciled, filed or closed. Obtain the current status and supporting evidence from the CFO and accountant.

## Access to detailed information

Accounting files, private correspondence and case-specific tax advice are held separately from this handbook. Ask the CFO or leadership for access to the relevant restricted records.


# Plan the finance cycle

Keep recurring work visible without maintaining conflicting calendars.

#### During the week

Review incoming transfers, liquidity by entity and currency, ready-to-pay requests, incomplete expenses, failed payments, support cases and provider disputes. Track expected grants with the project owner.

Plan transfers needed to fund payout accounts before execution. USD movements can require additional lead time; use current bank instructions and observed status rather than a guaranteed arrival time.

#### Payment sessions

OCE executes a submitted expense within seven business days after it has been approved by a collective administrator. This timeframe concerns execution by OCE, not receipt of the funds in the beneficiary’s bank account.

A problem preventing payment, such as missing documentation or an inconsistency requiring resolution, may extend this timeframe. Inform the requester of the blocking issue and the information or action needed to resolve it.

Monday and Thursday are the usual historical processing days. They are an internal working rhythm, not a guarantee of payment on a particular weekday; the seven-business-day rule is the reference.

#### Monthly

**By the 25th of each month at the latest:** Ivan completes salary processing through SD Worx and meal-voucher processing through Edenred (€10 face value per voucher), planning earlier where necessary so salaries are received before month-end. Verify submission and payment/order status; escalate any threatened deadline to JF. Follow the [payroll and meal-voucher procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/payroll-expense-processing).

Prepare bank/platform evidence and the unresolved-item list for financial review. Check grant allocations, reporting deadlines and, for the applicable host, GitHub Sponsors allocation reports. Reuse the existing finance meeting and records.

#### Quarterly

Prepare [accounting records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting), review outstanding reconciliation items and confirm the period-close instructions with the CFO and accountant.

#### Handover

Each open item needs an owner, next action and date. Before absence, verify the backup’s authority and access. Do not rely on a static statement that someone can always take over.

The professionalisation plan’s financial pack and continuity test remain separate deliverables requiring evidence.

#### Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identifies A03, V01 and V11. JF confirmed A03 on 14 September 2026 as recorded in Payment sessions. V01 and V11 remain subject to their respective validations. Record the approved text and effective date before changing the corresponding operating rule.


# Match incoming bank transfers

Record the actual receipt against the correct entity, currency and collective.

#### Inputs

Use [Forms of support and administrative contributions](/oc-europe-internal-doc/the-foundation/forms-of-support-and-administrative-contributions) for the funding classification, default calculation base, costs and cancellation rules approved on 19 October 2026. Particular agreements and valid amendments remain applicable; resolve conflicting terms before allocation. The two manual grant entries below remain required.

Use the bank transaction, contribution order or grant reference, intended collective and supporting correspondence. Check whether the receipt is already represented by an automated platform entry before adding funds.

#### Match an existing contribution

In the host dashboard’s bank-sync workflow, locate the bank transaction and matching contribution. Compare reference, amount, currency and recipient before using **Match**.

#### Allocate an identifiable receipt without an order

For a grant or other identifiable receipt, use the supported **Add Funds** route after checking the agreement and actual bank receipt. Record the reference and a short internal explanation. Verify the resulting entry and avoid duplicating an existing allocation.

**Grant receipt checklist: net allocation and administrative contribution**

**Owner:** Ivan is responsible and accountable for allocating an identified receipt under [RACI line 26](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle). Laura supplies or clarifies the grant purpose, conditions and dossier and organises an authorised replacement when needed. CFO handles financial discrepancies and reconciliation review. Routine allocation within the agreed terms does not require a new prior approval from CFO or JF.

1. **Identify the receipt and beneficiary.** Confirm that funds have actually arrived, using the bank transaction/date/reference, amount and currency. Match the funder, grant and tranche to the exact collective, legal host/entity and currency. Do not infer the beneficiary from a similar project or programme name. Check both the collective and operating-budget records for an existing automated or manual entry, including a fee already recorded.
2. **Read the signed Mandate Agreement.** Open the current signed mandate and any valid, applicable documented amendment or grant-specific agreement. Verify the administrative contribution percentage, its calculation base (not automatically the net bank receipt), fixed fee if applicable, currency, timing, instalment treatment, caps and any approved exemption or exception. Check compatibility with the funding conditions. Record the clause/version and calculation in the restricted grant record. Do not substitute a generic platform/default rate, an unsigned template or a previous grant's rate. Missing or conflicting terms must be resolved before finalising the affected allocation.
3. **Calculate and document the split.** Distinguish the grant amount stated by the funder, cash actually credited to the bank, charges already withheld, separately charged bank costs, and any executed currency conversion. Calculate the administrative contribution from the contractual base and rate, or the documented fixed amount, and identify the amount due for this tranche. Deduct a cost from the collective only where the applicable agreement or approved rule provides for that treatment; do not invent who bears an unexplained difference. Follow the executed-conversion rule below and never deduct the same bank/conversion cost twice. If a fee is denominated in a different currency, record the applicable documented conversion basis; ask CFO to resolve an unspecified treatment rather than treating an indicative spot rate as an executed conversion.
4. **Credit the collective with the net amount.** Use **Add Funds** for the amount allocated to the collective after its applicable administrative contribution and other documented deductions. Verify the exact collective/host/currency before saving. Record the funder, grant/tranche and bank reference in the appropriate fields and a clear description. Preserve the funder's restrictions and the required donor visibility.
5. **Manually add the fee we retain to OUR operating budget on Open Collective.** This workflow requires **TWO SEPARATE MANUAL Add Funds entries**:

   * **Entry 1 — beneficiary collective:** manually add the net grant amount to the beneficiary collective's budget, as in step 4.
   * **Entry 2 — OUR operating budget:** open OCE's operating budget on Open Collective and manually use **Add Funds** to add the actual fee amount we retain (the administrative contribution). This credits our operating budget with that amount. Use the operating budget belonging to the relevant legal entity and currency (for example, OCEF EUR or OCEF USD), not the beneficiary collective's budget.

   **Deducting the fee from the collective's grant is not enough. Writing the fee in a description or internal note is not enough. Ivan must also create and verify the separate Add Funds entry for the fee on OUR operating budget.** The platform does not do this automatically in this grant workflow; do not use its automatic host-fee module to collect the same fee again.

   **Illustration only — not a standard fee rate:** if EUR 10,000 is received and the signed agreement sets a 5% administrative contribution on that amount, with no bank charges or currency conversion in this example, manually add **EUR 9,500 to the beneficiary collective** AND manually add **EUR 500 to OUR operating budget**. The two entries together account for the EUR 10,000 received.

   Verify that neither manual entry incurs another automatic fee. Do not change general host settings to solve one receipt: if the supported entry route would apply a fee again, stop and resolve that route before completing it. Record the administrative contribution once, with the same grant/tranche reference and a reference to the collective allocation. If a documented exemption makes it zero, record that fact in the dossier rather than inventing fee income.
6. **Verify both saved entries and reconcile.** Read back the transaction IDs/links, amounts, currencies, destination budgets and resulting balances. The two entries split one receipt; the operating-budget entry is not a second external receipt. In a single reconciliation currency, the net collective allocation plus the administrative contribution plus any separately documented costs charged to this receipt must equal the actual amount available before those costs. If starting from the bank's already-net credit or net executed-conversion proceeds, do not add previously withheld costs again. Explain any difference and retain the conversion bridge where currencies differ. Do not force the figures to match or declare the receipt fully allocated while one required entry is missing.
7. **Close the operational record.** Link the bank receipt, signed agreement/clause, calculation, cost/FX evidence, both platform entries and appropriate supporting documents in the existing grant dossier and tracking application. Keep sensitive supporting material in restricted records; do not put bank details, signatures or private agreement content in public descriptions. Record the processing date and operator, update the grant/tranche status, and inform Laura/the collective through the established workflow. Give the designated financial reviewer the evidence needed for reconciliation review; operational completion is not independent financial validation.

If one entry succeeds and the other fails or its result is uncertain, record that partial state and inspect the platform history before retrying. Complete or correct only the missing/incorrect entry through the supported route, keeping the audit trail; do not repeat both entries.

For a missing agreement, beneficiary or funding-condition question, contact Laura. For a calculation, fee-currency, cost-allocation or reconciliation discrepancy, contact CFO. A new contribution exception or material departure goes to JF under the existing RACI. Record the blocker, owner and next action; no new fee rate, monetary threshold or blanket approval requirement is created by this checklist.

#### Resolve discrepancies

Do not assume that a receipt in an EUR account belongs to an EUR collective, or that an expected amount equals the amount received. Record the actual movement, apply the currency rule below and obtain the appropriate decision for any other unusual route before finalising.

The legacy pages cite Zoho and platform Bank Sync inconsistently. Confirm the current workflow with the financial owner before changing the official accounting or reconciliation record.

#### Currency conversion

When incoming funds are in a different currency from the collective, execute an actual conversion into the collective’s currency when processing the receipt, in either direction, including USD to EUR and EUR to USD. Credit the collective with the net amount actually obtained from the executed conversion, not a notional amount calculated from an indicative daily rate. The collective bears the conversion costs included in that operation; do not deduct those same costs a second time. Retain the conversion evidence, including the date, applied rate, source amount and net amount received.

It does not replace the separate work on the Foundation’s wider foreign-exchange risk policy.

#### Unidentified receipts

Search the order, correspondence and existing project records. If the destination remains unclear, follow hold and investigate funds. Do not treat elapsed time as authority for reallocation.

#### Completion evidence

Keep the bank reference, platform entry, collective, currency, review and any correction linked. Verify the credited balance and donor visibility setting.

#### Source and review

Grant-allocation checklist clarified at JF's request on 19 October 2026: signed mandate verification, net collective allocation and separate manual administrative contribution to the operating budget. Existing RACI, contract terms and approved currency rule remain applicable.

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identifies A08, V03 and V11. The A08 incoming-funds conversion rule was approved on 14 September 2026 above. V03 and V11 remain subject to their respective validations. Record the approved text and effective date before changing the corresponding operating rule.


# Process outgoing payments

Review the request, execute once and verify the final record.

## 1. Identify the request

Open the host dashboard’s **Outgoing money → Pay disbursements** workflow. Confirm host, collective, currency and request type: reimbursement, invoice or grant.

“Ready to pay” is a platform status. It does not establish that OCE’s documentation and risk checks are complete.

## 2. Review evidence and approvals

* Collective or fund approval is present.
* Purpose and amount match the activity and supporting documents.
* A reimbursement has a valid receipt; a partial claim is explained.
* An invoice identifies the issuer, recipient, amount and applicable tax information.
* A grant has the documentation required for its approved route.
* Legal recipient and payout information are consistent.
* No duplicate or unresolved earlier payment attempt exists.

Use the instructions for the actual arrangement. Internal Foundation expenses and standard hosted-collective invoices may have different addressees. Ask for financial or legal clarification instead of applying a universal invoice rule.

## 3. Resolve missing information

Mark an incomplete request appropriately and explain the specific correction. A blocking issue may extend the seven-business-day execution timeframe; inform the requester of the issue and the information or action required. See [the payment timetable](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/financial-ops-task-overview). Keep personal documents and sensitive explanations in private fields. If grantee and payee differ, obtain the documented approval required for that route.

## 4. Confirm liquidity and payout method

Check the correct Wise, PayPal or bank account and the current payout instructions. For Foundation Wise top-ups, follow the current **Add funds** instructions for the selected currency and verify the destination before the bank transfer. Do not reuse old screenshots as bank instructions.

Direct bank payments need the current request’s approval, complete details and a plan for recording the outcome. A previous direct payment is not a general exception.

## 5. Execute and verify

Use the supported route once. If the result is uncertain, inspect the bank/provider status before retrying. Do not combine a manual payment with an automated attempt for the same request.

Record the confirmed payment reference and update the platform if the route requires manual recording. Check the amount, currency and final status. A technical error is not proof that no transfer occurred.

## 6. Close or hand over

Retain evidence and unresolved actions. Follow reconciliation for differences. The payment timetable is maintained in the finance cycle, not duplicated here.

## Evidence at each handover

| Stage     | Evidence to retain in the restricted operational record                         |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Intake    | Expense link, collective/host, recipient, amount and currency.                  |
| Review    | Applicable documents, collective approval and any required additional decision. |
| Execution | The chosen route and confirmed provider or bank reference.                      |
| Follow-up | Reconciliation result, unresolved difference and next responsible person.       |

Use the current authorised responsibility matrix. This checklist clarifies the handover; it does not create a new payment delegation or settle pending policy decisions.

If someone reports “paid but not received”, compare the platform record with the provider or bank outcome before deciding on a further attempt. Keep the existing request as the reference. Explain the next check to the requester without disclosing internal controls or another person’s information.

For changes in the expense form, consult the [official submission guide](https://documentation.opencollective.com/expenses-and-getting-paid/submitting-expenses). Verify which functions are available for the actual host rather than assuming that every platform option is supported.

## Source and review

# Allocate GitHub Sponsors receipts

Use the payout report and distinguish the OSE route from OCEF.

The existing detailed workflow identifies the GitHub Sponsors payout as an **OSE** receipt. Keep this reference for team coordination; it does not establish an active OCEF route.

## Monthly workflow

1. Confirm the applicable host and receiving account.
2. Obtain the relevant payout report from the authorised [GitHub fiscal-host dashboard](https://github.com/sponsors/hello-europe/dashboard/fiscal_host).
3. Match the report period and total to the actual receipt.
4. Coordinate the supported allocation process with the platform operations team.
5. Check every resulting collective allocation and the total before marking the task complete.

The older procedure names a Spring 2026 contact and anticipates a future tool. Confirm the current owner and tool rather than treating either statement as permanent.

## Evidence

Save the report in the [existing restricted folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xvOWbvDs9OF0XTmK5XOC6BORoyUhQL4W) and link the receipt, allocation and discrepancies. Do not allocate without the report or create a second entry for funds already recorded.

For a new connection request, check the host and current route before giving instructions.


# Process payroll and meal vouchers

Process monthly salaries and meal vouchers by the 25th and retain the supporting records.

The existing internal procedure records Belgian payroll administration through SD Worx. Confirm the current employment arrangement and access before handling a payroll task.

#### Payroll preparation

JF supplies or approves payroll inputs and any changes to employment terms or remuneration. **Ivan is responsible for the monthly operational processing and submission of salaries through SD Worx**, using the approved inputs and authorised payment process.

#### Monthly deadline: no later than the 25th

**Ivan must complete salary processing through SD Worx and meal-voucher processing through Edenred no later than the 25th of each month.** The objective is for employees to receive their salaries before the end of the month. Plan earlier when provider/bank processing times or non-working days require it; the 25th is the latest internal deadline, not the day to start preparation.

1. Collect and check the approved monthly payroll inputs in time for processing.
2. Complete the required SD Worx submissions and salary-payment steps using the authorised process. Verify the actual payroll and bank status before assuming that payment has been made or initiating any further transfer.
3. Process the month's meal vouchers through **Edenred**, with a **face value of €10 per meal voucher**, using the applicable approved number of vouchers for each employee. This is the voucher face value, not a statement of the employer's contribution.
4. Check submission/order confirmations, any required funding and the expected execution dates. Follow up rejected, pending or failed instructions promptly.
5. Retain dated evidence in restricted payroll/HR records. If missing inputs, access or another blocker threatens the deadline or month-end salary receipt, notify JF immediately and coordinate financial issues with CFO.

#### Absence coverage

Before planned leave affecting this monthly cycle, Ivan must hand over the SD Worx and Edenred tasks to an explicitly designated, authorised backup with verified individual access, approved inputs and clear deadlines. Naming someone as backup does not itself grant access or authority. The proposed role-backup policy remains subject to adoption.

#### Platform record

Ivan records the monthly operational payroll expense using the appropriate summary and allocation. Match it to the payroll evidence and confirmed payment, and avoid duplicate entries.

#### Privacy

Keep individual payslips, salary details and personal identifiers in restricted HR records. Use a neutral public title if an aggregated platform entry is required. Do not assume an expense is private merely because it is an internal operating cost.

#### Period-end

Use [quarterly accounting records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting) for the SD Worx evidence needed for the period. Resolve accounting treatment through the competent financial and payroll contacts.


# Reconcile bank, platform and accounting records

Explain every difference and retain evidence of the review.

#### Prepare the period

Define entity, currency, accounts and cutoff. Collect bank/provider statements, platform exports, agreements and supporting documents. Distinguish project funds from OCE operating funds and verify the treatment of internal funds such as GSF.

For each movement recorded on Open Collective, attach an invoice or another appropriate supporting document. Use the document suited to the movement and keep sensitive evidence in the appropriate restricted record. Track missing supporting documents in the existing reconciliation record.

#### Match the records

1. Compare opening balances and incoming receipts with platform contributions and allocations.
2. Compare outgoing bank movements with paid requests and their evidence.
3. Identify duplicates, missing entries, timing differences, currency differences and unidentified items.
4. Check transfers between accounts separately so they are not counted as new income or spending.
5. Reconcile the result to the accounting record through the agreed financial review.

#### Investigate differences

Keep each unresolved item with its reference, amount, currency, explanation, owner, next action and date. Do not force a match simply to clear a list. Correct the operational record only with the appropriate evidence and retain the audit trail.

#### Review and output

The documented role model separates Ivan’s preparation from CFO’s financial control and accounting coordination with Saïd. The consolidated audit asks for validation of the full procedure and system map. CFO is the accountable reviewer; confirm the current system and retain review evidence before declaring the reconciliation complete.

The output is a reconciled period or an explicitly qualified result with unresolved items. A sample check of a few collectives is not a full reconciliation.

See [unidentified funds](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/unclaimed-or-unreconciliable-funds) and [quarterly records](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting).

# Handle refunds and disputes

Verify the original transaction, authority and provider status before acting.

#### Intake

Identify the transaction, requester, collective, entity, amount, currency and reason. Check whether a provider dispute is already open and record its actual deadline.

#### Review

Gather the original contribution, payment evidence and relevant correspondence. Confirm the applicable agreement and current provider options. Do not issue a blanket legal statement that every donation is non-refundable.

#### Decision

All OCE team members are authorised to approve and carry out refunds to donors. Prior approval from CFO or JF is not required. This authority does not remove the transaction checks and recording requirements below. Escalate material, repeated or suspected-fraud cases appropriately.

#### Execute and record

Use the approved refund route and check for an existing refund or disputed transaction first. Avoid a separate payment that could duplicate a provider refund or chargeback. Record the reference, actual outcome and the effect on the platform and bank records.

#### Provider-specific follow-up

* PayPal disputes.
* Stripe disputes.
* Stripe bank debits.

Use case-specific communication and do not promise timing from an old template. Keep sensitive evidence in the restricted case record.

#### Source and review

Decision confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026: all OCE team members are authorised to approve and carry out donor refunds without prior approval from CFO or JF. This resolves the refund-authority question raised in audit V04; it does not constitute specialist validation of every provider-specific dispute procedure.

Signing powers, access and specialist validations remain separate.


# Banking, access and continuity

Verify accounts and authority in the restricted inventory before acting.

## Account purpose

OCE workflows use KBC for Foundation banking, Wise for applicable payouts and internal cards, PayPal for applicable contributions and payments, and Stripe through the platform. Exact accounts, entities, currency routes and permissions must be checked in the current inventory.

The [access inventory](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/191GVeQ3Xit_n_IYVIPd6iQpBjFa2re88/edit) and professionalisation workstream J1-02 are the starting references. A list in this handbook is not proof that access or a delegation is current.

## Before a payment or top-up

Confirm account owner, legal entity, currency, available balance and authorised operator. Use current bank instructions. For an unusual movement or unclear financial treatment, obtain the competent decision before execution.

## Access changes

Record the business need and obtain the required approval. Use individual access and appropriate authentication. Verify what was granted and remove obsolete access through the authorised process.

Keep passwords, recovery codes, signing credentials and authentication links out of GitBook.

## Continuity

Confirm a backup’s access and authority before relying on it. The plan asks for evidence of continuity and a later absence test; an old statement that recovery arrangements exist does not prove they have been tested.

## Signing authority

Use a restricted, dated record of powers and entity coverage. Do not rely on static Board or bank-user names in a procedure.

# Prepare quarterly accounting records

Assemble period evidence and obtain the financial review before closure.

#### Scope

Prepare evidence for OCEF EUR and USD, distinguishing Foundation operating activity, hosted collectives and internal funds such as GSF. Platform categories do not themselves determine the legal or tax treatment.

#### Responsibility and VAT follow-up

Ivan owns the collection and preparation of accounting documents, including supporting records for operational expenses charged to OCEF budgets. He follows up on missing pieces and makes the accounting pack available to Saïd, keeping the CFO informed.

For each VAT period, Ivan follows the process through to completion:

1. Confirm the document collection deadline, filing deadline and payment instructions with Saïd.
2. Assemble and transmit the supporting documents, and track missing items until resolved.
3. Obtain the filing confirmation and acknowledgement from Saïd for the correct entity and period.
4. Follow up on any payment due, arranging execution through the existing authorised banking process and verifying its outcome. This responsibility does not grant additional payment or approval authority.
5. Retain the filing and payment evidence in the restricted accounting records, with any outstanding issue, next action and responsible person clearly recorded.

Saïd remains responsible for accounting work and returns within his engagement. The CFO reviews the supporting evidence and outstanding issues and coordinates accounting instructions and conclusions. Ivan escalates missing confirmations, unclear instructions or a deadline at risk to the CFO; if the CFO is unavailable, escalate to JF so that follow-up is assigned.

#### Documents to assemble

* SD Worx invoices and accounting documents from eDox.
* Billit invoices in PDF and XML, plus the requested quarter data.
* Statements for the relevant KBC project and operating accounts, Wise EUR/USD and PayPal EUR/USD.
* Platform transaction exports for the same period and scope.
* Supporting invoices, reimbursement notes and explanations of unresolved differences.

#### File preparation

Use the [existing accounting folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XTFPtsXH0rhCvyzbuEFkeiSV6zCGUzxa). Keep one invoice per item and avoid combined PDFs that obscure individual documents. Store invoices in the appropriate Bills section and statements/exports in the period’s bank and platform reports.

For internal card expenses, check that the document names the Foundation where required. Do not apply the standard hosted-collective invoice addressee to OCE’s own operating activity.

#### Review

Match the period, accounts, totals and supporting records. Keep unresolved items visible for the financial reviewer. CFO owns financial review and coordination with Saïd; obtain and retain the applicable review before describing the period as closed.

#### Late documents and corrections

Do not silently change a closed folder or decide a new accounting period for a late invoice. Preserve the original document date, record when it was received and obtain the accountant’s treatment through the agreed route. Keep any correction traceable.

#### Completion evidence

Retain the prepared pack, review findings, corrections or reservations, and dated closure/filing confirmation as applicable. Preparation of accounts and governance approval are separate events.

The [consolidated audit](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1L-xi_oBqx5osXoe_jaa4TXNSx-oZtYqA/edit) identifies V01, V02 and V11 as requiring a decision or specialist validation. # Respond to a PayPal dispute

Work from the live provider case and retain the evidence submitted.

## Open and identify

Verify the notification in the authorised PayPal account. Record the case identifier, affected transaction, current status and response deadline shown in the case. Do not rely on the old handbook’s fixed ten-day assumption.

## Prepare the response

Match the transaction to the platform contribution and collective. Gather the relevant record, contribution description and correspondence. Explain the transaction accurately without adding claims that the evidence does not support.

## Submit through the approved route

Follow the case’s current instructions and the applicable internal approval. Do not initiate a separate refund merely because a dispute has opened; first establish how it would interact with the live case.

## Follow the outcome

Save the submitted evidence and confirmation. Track the provider’s decision and any bank or balance movement. Update the support record and reconciliation evidence without duplicating the transaction.

Escalate suspected misuse, recurring cases or material exposure through [refunds and disputes](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/refunds-and-disputes).


# Respond to a Stripe dispute

Coordinate the platform case and track the financial outcome.

## Verify the case

Locate the provider notification and corresponding platform contribution. Record the case reference, reason, entity, amount, deadline and person responsible for responding.

## Coordinate the response

Use the authorised platform/payment support route where direct Stripe access is not available. Supply the contribution record and relevant evidence. Do not open parallel donor negotiations or a separate refund without coordinating how it affects the dispute.

## Track to completion

Retain the submitted evidence, provider outcome and any balance or bank movement. Update the platform and restricted support record as applicable. A lost dispute, a voluntary refund and a bank debit must remain distinguishable in the evidence.

For a debit from the connected bank, follow [Stripe bank debits](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/stripe-bank-debit-in-case-of-refunds). Escalate recurring or material cases through [the refund procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/refunds-and-disputes).


# Investigate a Stripe bank debit

Match a debit to its provider event before classifying it.

A Stripe-related bank debit can relate to a refund or another provider balance event. Do not classify it from the bank label alone.

## Check the evidence

1. Identify the date, amount, currency and bank reference.
2. Obtain the related Stripe or platform event through the authorised route.
3. Match it to the original contribution, refund or dispute.
4. Check whether the effect is already recorded on the platform.
5. Retain the evidence and obtain the correct accounting treatment.

## If it does not match

Keep the item unresolved in the reconciliation record with an owner and next action. Do not describe an unexplained debit as routine or create a duplicate expense to make totals agree.

See [reconciliation](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/reconciliation-process) and [refunds and disputes](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/refunds-and-disputes).


# Hold and investigate unidentified funds

Keep received money traceable while its destination remains unresolved.

## Internal 24-month rule

Operational decision confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026: after 24 months, carry out a final search for the intended beneficiary. If the beneficiary remains unidentified after that final search, apply the reallocation procedure below for Open Collective Europe's operating budget, subject to the applicable agreement, law, funding restrictions and required approvals.

## Investigate and track

Check platform orders, bank references, grant records and relevant correspondence. Where appropriate, ask the likely donor or collective for evidence through a private channel. Keep received funds distinguishable from available operating money while investigation is ongoing.

Record the receipt date, amount, currency, account, reference, research performed, owner and next review action. Document the final search and its outcome before recording any reallocation. Retain the receipt, decision and resulting platform and accounting entries. If the intended collective is identified, verify and record the correct allocation.

## Contractual scope

The [published hosting template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/e/2PACX-1vS2jTb55T-kXHDPLNWVg4xUuMGmediT9VBqwsNpdQA8geRpcPsyYvfPggwJ6iZaPw/pub) reviewed on 24 September 2026 contains an explicit unidentified-contributions provision: 24 months from receipt, a documented final search and possible reallocation to the Foundation’s general operating budget if the beneficiary remains unidentified, subject to applicable law, donor restrictions and required third-party approvals.

It separately addresses identified inactive initiatives and their termination procedure. Do not apply the unidentified-contributions rule to a known collective’s remaining balance. Before relying on a new provision for an existing arrangement, check the applicable version, notification and effective-date requirements. Presence in the published template is not proof of legal validation or notification to every existing initiative.

## Source and review

Operational decision: JF, 14 September 2026. Published contract provisions checked on 24 September 2026. The rule remains subject to applicable law, funding restrictions and required approvals.


# Use internal virtual cards

Authorisation, use, evidence and follow-up for OCE payment cards.

#### Policy

Virtual cards are an **internal OCE payment tool**. They are not offered, issued or made available to hosted collectives.

There is no standard or exceptional request route through which a hosted collective can obtain a virtual card.

OCE may use virtual cards only for:

* recurring or one-off operating expenses of the Foundation;
* internal infrastructure, software and administrative costs;
* internal OCE projects or funds, including the Global Statelessness Fund (GSF), where the card remains legally and operationally an OCE payment instrument.

#### Authorization and setup

Before a new internal virtual card is created:

1. The functional owner documents the business purpose, budget, proposed cardholder, spending limit and expected duration.
2. CFO validates the financial controls, documentation requirements and reconciliation treatment.
3. JF approves the creation of the card and any material subsequent change.
4. Ivan creates or configures the card in Wise after approval and records the relevant operational information.

A card must not be created or materially changed without the required validation and approval.

#### Use and documentation

* Each card has a named cardholder and an approved purpose.
* The card may only be used within the approved budget, limits and scope.
* It must not be shared with another person.
* The cardholder must obtain and provide a valid invoice or receipt for every transaction.
* Where applicable, the invoice must identify Open Collective Europe Foundation as the customer.
* Each transaction and its supporting document must be recorded promptly in the appropriate internal workflow or Open Collective budget.
* Approval flows must avoid self-approval wherever the platform or process provides an approval step.

#### Monitoring and irregularities

* Ivan performs the first-line operational monitoring of card transactions and requests missing supporting documents.
* CFO owns financial control, reconciliation and the accounting treatment coordinated with Saïd.
* For the GSF card, Laura coordinates operational follow-up with Sabine and Elif, including receipt collection and budget tracking.
* Missing documentation, use outside the approved purpose or any other anomaly must be documented and corrected promptly.
* Repeated non-compliance, suspected misuse or material financial exposure is escalated to JF.

Any future change to the internal-only policy requires an explicit organization-level decision by JF. It must not be introduced through a one-off exception for a hosted collective.

#### Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. Existing policy text retained and edited for structure. Editorial review does not establish a new approval date or delegation.


# Risk and escalation

Describe the actual concern, protect the evidence and obtain the right decision.

#### When to use this process

Use it when an application, transaction, agreement or new fact creates an unresolved legal, financial, safeguarding or reputational concern.

#### Prepare the review

Record the facts, source dates, affected entity and activity, potential impact, missing evidence, options and the decision needed. Separate an allegation from a verified finding.

Use relevant official sources and specialist advice for legal or sanctions questions. A screening result requires examination; a name match alone is not a final conclusion.

#### Route the concern

* Project design and operational coordination: involve Laura.
* Financial treatment or control: involve CFO.
* Material executive commitments or risk: involve JF and the Board where reserved authority applies.
* Safety or misconduct: use [safeguarding response](/oc-europe-internal-doc/human-resources-introduction/detailed-guidance-for-staff-on-responding-to-safeguarding-issues), including an alternative contact if the usual one is involved.

Name the case owner under the adopted RACI; escalation does not transfer ongoing ownership.

#### While a decision is pending

Pause the affected commitment or payment if its basis is unresolved. Continue unaffected information gathering and record the next action. Do not treat a high amount, a redirection or an incomplete file alone as a nonstandard exception.

#### Decision record

Retain the decision, authority, reasons, scope, conditions and review date. A restriction, closure or reallocation needs its own basis; see [freezing and closure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/freezing-collectives) and [unidentified funds](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/unclaimed-or-unreconciliable-funds).

Keep case evidence in the restricted register and Drive. This handbook explains the method, not a list of sensitive cases.

#### Source and review

Checked on 24 September 2026. Operational responsibilities, inactivity procedure and non-partisan advocacy policy were adopted on 14 September. Specialist validation, access review and case-specific decisions remain separate; see [documentation decisions and remaining validations](/oc-europe-internal-doc/tools-and-platforms-used-at-oce/brand).

#### Operational responsibility reference — 14 September 2026

Use the [RACI adopted on 14 September 2026](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle) and [current-source question guide](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/question-chatgpt). Signing powers, access and specialist validations remain separate.

# Environmental commitments

Practical measures for OCE operations and relevant grant activities.

**Approved by:** Executive Director **Review cycle:** Annual, or earlier following a material change in activities or applicable requirements

## Purpose

Open Collective Europe Foundation (“OCE”) recognises that responsible grant-making and organisational management include limiting negative environmental impacts and supporting sustainable development. This policy establishes the environmental principles and practices applicable to OCE’s own operations and, where relevant and proportionate, to the grant-making and re-granting programmes it administers.

## Scope

This policy applies to OCE employees, contractors and operational activities under OCE’s direct control. Hosted collectives and grantees remain responsible for their own operations and compliance, but OCE may incorporate proportionate environmental considerations into due diligence, contracting and monitoring where relevant to the funded activity or donor requirements.

## Commitments

OCE commits to:

* Comply with applicable environmental laws, regulations and contractual requirements.
* Prevent pollution and minimise waste and unnecessary resource consumption.
* Consider environmental impacts in operational, travel and purchasing decisions.
* Promote practical, proportionate improvements that reflect OCE’s size, digital operating model and international activities.
* Review environmental performance and improve this policy over time.

## Operational measures

## Digital-first working

OCE prioritises electronic records, signatures, communications and reporting. Printing should be avoided unless legally or operationally necessary. Digital storage, equipment and digital resources should be managed efficiently, with obsolete or duplicate data removed where appropriate and lawful.

## Travel

Remote participation should be considered when it can achieve the same operational purpose. When travel is necessary, staff should favour lower-emission transport, including rail over air travel where practical, combine meetings when possible and avoid unnecessary journeys.

## Procurement and equipment

When purchasing resources, OCE should consider durability, repairability, energy efficiency, expected lifespan, packaging and the supplier’s environmental practices alongside quality and operational requirements. Equipment should be reused or repaired where feasible and disposed of through appropriate recycling channels, with secure data removal.

## Grant-making and re-granting

For grants with potentially material environmental impacts, OCE may apply risk-based screening and request evidence of compliance with applicable environmental requirements. Environmental conditions or reporting may be included where relevant to the programme, the funded activity or donor expectations. OCE seeks to support activities that advance the Sustainable Development Goals while avoiding disproportionate administrative burdens for small or grassroots organisations.

## Monitoring and accountability

The Executive Director is responsible for implementation of this policy. Team members are responsible for applying it within their areas of work and reporting material concerns or non-compliance.

At least annually, OCE will review:

* Material business travel and opportunities to reduce it.
* Significant equipment purchases, reuse and disposal.
* Material environmental risks identified in directly managed programmes.
* Actions taken and practical objectives for the following year.

Any significant environmental incident connected to OCE’s direct operations must be documented and escalated to the Executive Director.

## Review

This policy will be reviewed at least annually. Updates will be approved by the Executive Director and communicated to the team.

## Source and review

Editorial review: 11 September 2026. Existing policy text retained and edited for structure. Editorial review does not establish a new approval date or delegation.


# Review advocacy and political activity

Use a case-specific legal review where the boundary is unclear.

## Policy

Decision confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026: OCE permits non-partisan advocacy on a cause, including advocacy concerning legislation or public policy, while excluding support for political parties or candidates. The subject of a cause alone is not grounds for exclusion. Activities must remain consistent with OCE's public-benefit purpose and applicable law.

## Apply the distinction

Review the actual activity, intended use of funds, public messaging and relationships with parties, candidates or elections. If the boundary is unclear, escalate to JF for the appropriate review before accepting a commitment or applying an enforcement action. This policy decision does not constitute legal approval of every proposed activity.

## Record the outcome

Keep the scope, decision, any conditions and relevant review evidence in the restricted case record. For a proposed restriction or closure, use [the separate procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/support-ops/freezing-collectives).

## Source and review

Operational policy confirmed by JF on 14 September 2026, addressing audit V06. The earlier blanket prohibition on influencing legislation or public policy is superseded by the distinction above. The hosting agreements' broader apolitical wording should be aligned separately; no contract amendment is recorded by this GitBook update.


# Team and responsibilities

Reference for team roles, decisions and day-to-day guidance.

**Operational reference adopted by JF on 14 September 2026. Handbook owner: Laura.**

#### Find what to do and whom to contact

Start with the [operational RACI adopted on 14 September 2026](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle) to identify the accountable person, the person doing the work and the escalation route. Then consult the relevant procedure and case records. [Ask ChatGPT a question: prompt and examples](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/question-chatgpt).

| Person                                                                                                                 | Role                                  | When to contact them                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [JF](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/executive-director-jf)                               | Executive direction                   | Strategy, resources, exceptions, material commitments and the Board                                                        |
| [Laura](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/strategic-projects-and-operations-lead-laura)     | Projects and operational coordination | Initial triage of all applications, admission within the established framework, projects, reports and operational blockers |
| [Ivan](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/financial-operations-and-platform-specialist-ivan) | Financial and platform operations     | Routine payments, support, first-level checks, evidence and access                                                         |
| [CFO](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/cfo-budget-and-financial-control)                   | Financial control                     | Internal budget, forecasts, figures, reconciliation and accounting coordination; no project contact                        |
| [Saïd](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/accountant-said)                                   | Accounting work                       | Work within his engagement, coordinated by CFO; factual exchanges with contributors are possible                           |
| Lucas                                                                                                                  | OSE liaison                           | Misdirected open-source projects referred by Laura to Open Source Europe                                                   |

#### Project contacts and continuity

Laura coordinates projects and operational follow-up; Ivan handles payment and platform operations. Project and collective communications remain with the operational team. Required financial reviews must have a designated qualified reviewer. JF resolves any gap in review coverage; this does not transfer technical validation or routine case ownership to JF.

#### Rules that avoid unnecessary back-and-forth

Laura assigns an owner to every application. Ivan or an authorised substitute executes complete routine payments without systematic prior approval from CFO. Any team member may approve and execute a routine donor refund, with checks and an audit trail. CFO coordinates accounting; Laura and Ivan may participate in factual exchanges with Saïd. JF decides genuine exceptions and material commitments.

The owner retains responsibility for follow-up after an escalation. Responsibility for a process does not automatically confer signing authority or bank access. Reserved matters remain with the Board.

#### Authoritative reference and older versions

For operational responsibilities, the adopted GitBook RACI above takes precedence over conflicting assignments in the [August spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Z2Jd_fMR3-tE0GBT2WN_UXdzVHSBEHroN2RtDuiZ-9k/edit). The plan dated 22 September states that its main discrepancies have been aligned. GitBook remains the operational reference; check the date and scope before reusing an older copy. Old audit notes stating “RACI to be confirmed” must not reopen this allocation of responsibilities.

Adoption does not close specialist tax, financial or legal validations, or the Organisation/Vendor policy decision. Consult the plan for deadlines: reconciliations have been deferred to cycle 2.


# JF — executive direction

Strategy, governance and decisions on material commitments.

JF sets organisational direction, priorities and resource allocation. He leads major institutional relationships and prepares matters requiring Board oversight or approval.

#### Core responsibilities

* Define priorities and assess whether new activities fit the mission and capacity.
* Review budgets, forecasts and material risks with the CFO.
* Make executive decisions within delegated authority.
* Prepare Board proposals and implement its decisions.
* Define roles, resolve capacity conflicts and address recurring ownership problems.

#### Decision boundaries

Material contractual, strategic, legal, reputational or resource commitments require the appropriate executive or Board decision. JF’s operational involvement does not replace the Board’s reserved authority.

Routine execution stays with its assigned owner. Escalating a case to JF does not automatically transfer its day-to-day management to him.

#### Prepare a decision

Give JF the facts, evidence, risk, available options, recommendation and required decision date. Record the decision, scope, conditions and follow-up owner in the restricted case record.

#### Expected outputs

Organisational priorities, approved decisions within authority, Board information, resource choices and clear delegations. Recurring escalations should lead to a process or capacity correction rather than permanent executive takeover.

#### Source and review

Operational responsibilities adopted by JF on 14 September 2026: [operational RACI adopted on 14 September 2026](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle). Specialist legal, tax and financial validations remain separate; the RACI does not establish signing powers or completion of professionalisation tasks.

# Ivan — financial and platform operations

Execute routine work with complete evidence and clear escalation.

Ivan prepares and executes routine financial and platform tasks under established procedures. He checks documents, payment details and approval status, and supplies operational evidence for financial control.

#### Core responsibilities

* Process monthly salaries through SD Worx and meal vouchers through Edenred (€10 face value each), **no later than the 25th of the month**, planning earlier as necessary for salary receipt before month-end. Verify completion and follow the [payroll and meal-voucher procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/payroll-expense-processing).
* Review receipts, invoices, grant documentation and payee information.
* Request missing or corrected information clearly.
* Execute documented, approved payments and record their outcome.
* Match identifiable incoming transfers and flag unresolved transactions.
* For grants, verify the signed mandate's administrative contribution, credit the collective net and manually record the contribution on the correct operating budget; verify both entries and their evidence using the [grant receipt checklist](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/bank-transfers-for-the-collectives#grant-receipt-checklist-net-allocation-and-administrative-contribution).
* Maintain platform notes and supporting records.
* Provide statements, exports and payment evidence to the CFO.
* Own accounting document collection and preparation, including supporting records for OCEF operating expenses, and follow up on missing pieces with Saïd.
* Track VAT filing and payment through to completion: obtain filing confirmations from Saïd, follow payment through the existing authorised banking process and retain the evidence for CFO review. Follow the [quarterly accounting procedure](/oc-europe-internal-doc/financial-operations-introduction/quarterly-accounting#responsibility-and-vat-follow-up).
* Carry out standard onboarding tasks when assigned.

#### Before acting

Use the operational checks. Pause the affected action when approval, identity, documentation or the payment route is unclear. A dashboard status alone does not complete OCE’s review.

#### Escalation

Take project-design questions to Laura, financial treatment to CFO and material executive matters to JF. Do not infer authority to accept an exception, sign a nonstandard agreement or validate a reconciliation from responsibility for execution.

#### Handover outputs

Keep a visible record of completed payments, blocked requests, unidentified transfers, corrections, next actions and their evidence. Confirm backup access before an absence.

#### Accounting coordination

The CFO coordinates accounting instructions and conclusions with Saïd. Laura and Ivan may exchange necessary factual information directly with Saïd while keeping CFO in the coordination loop. This is not authority to decide accounting treatment.

#### Source and review

Operational responsibilities adopted by JF on 14 September 2026: [operational RACI adopted on 14 September 2026](/oc-europe-internal-doc/meet-the-open-collective-europe-team/raci-operationnelle). Specialist legal, tax and financial validations remain separate; the RACI does not establish signing powers or completion of professionalisation tasks.

#### Operational responsibility reference — 14 September 2026

# Laura — projects and operational coordination

Turn fund and partnership commitments into workable processes.

Laura coordinates complex projects, strategic funds and operational partnerships. Her documented portfolio includes the Global Statelessness Fund, Ma Earth and Myriad USA.

#### Core responsibilities

* Translate agreements into milestones, tasks, owners and reporting dates.
* Coordinate programme contacts and internal contributors.
* Maintain the overview of open questions, decisions and dependencies.
* Prepare narrative reporting and obtain controlled financial information.
* Coordinate nonstandard workflows and structural platform requests.
* Document workable processes without duplicating case registers.

#### Fund-specific work

For GSF, coordinate grant delivery, documentation, budget tracking and reporting with the programme team. For Myriad USA, manage the operational relationship, grant requests and final reporting. For Ma Earth, work from the signed agreement; its legal characterisation remains a validation item in the audit.

#### Decision boundaries

Coordination does not itself authorise a financial treatment, material exception or signature. Obtain the relevant financial, legal or executive decision and retain its scope and conditions.

#### Working with Ivan and the internal finance function

Laura remains the project-facing coordinator. The CFO role provides internal budget and financial input without direct project contact. Laura obtains that input through the current finance route and communicates the outcome to the project.

Define the workflow before asking Ivan to execute it. Obtain financial control and reporting conclusions through the agreed financial route. Send JF concise decision notes when scope, risk or capacity exceeds the established arrangement.

#### Application triage

Laura reviews all incoming applications first and routes each one to herself, Ivan, or Lucas. She refers an open-source project to Lucas when it has applied to the wrong host and should apply to Open Source Europe. Record the resulting case owner.

# OCE operational RACI

**Internal reference adopted by JF on 14 September 2026. Document owner: Laura.**

This RACI establishes operational responsibilities based on the documentation and decisions approved by JF. It replaces conflicting assignments in the August matrix for day-to-day guidance. Legal signing powers, actual access rights and external providers' engagements must still be checked against their own records. Adoption of this RACI does not certify completion of tasks.

#### 1. Agreed organisational structure

| Person                                            | Main responsibility                                                                                                                                                      | Key boundary                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **JF — executive direction**                      | Strategy, budget and resources, major partnerships, policies, exceptions and material decisions; relationship with the Board.                                            | Does not become the routine case manager merely by making a decision on it.                                                                  |
| **Laura — operational coordination and projects** | Triage of all applications, admission within the established framework, allocation of work, complex funds, funder commitments and reports, risk and procedure follow-up. | Does not approve accounting or tax treatment in the competent financial reviewer's place; cannot independently extend a material commitment. |
| **Ivan — financial and platform operations**      | First-level checks, routine payments, allocation of identified receipts, support, delegated onboarding, records and access.                                              | Does not independently certify reconciliations or figures he prepares; does not decide a legal model or a substantial exception.             |
| **CFO**                                           | Reliable figures, reconciliations, financial review, budget and forecasts, control of fund flows, coordination with Saïd and financial advice.                           | Internal budget and finance role only; no direct contact with projects or collectives. Not a routine payment gate.                           |
| **Saïd — accountant**                             | Bookkeeping, preparation of returns and accounts, technical advice within his engagement.                                                                                | His scope depends on his actual engagement; the RACI does not automatically assign certification or an external audit.                       |
| **Board**                                         | Reserved governance decisions, oversight of executive direction, alternative route for conflicts involving JF.                                                           | Does not approve routine actions. Actual powers remain those of the applicable governance framework.                                         |
| **Lucas — Open Source Europe liaison**            | Receives open-source projects referred to OSE by Laura.                                                                                                                  | Does not approve OCEF operations; OSE admission and operations fall under OSE's own organisation.                                            |

Collectives and programme leads retain their programme decisions and the expense approvals specified in their agreements. The RACI below describes OCE's work; it does not transfer responsibility for all their activities to OCE.

#### 2. How to read the matrix

**A**: the person accountable for the outcome and decision within their scope. **R**: performs the work. **C**: consulted when the matter requires it. **I**: informed at the appropriate time, without prior approval.

In this matrix, CFO denotes the internal finance function. Required financial reviews must be assigned to a named, qualified person with the applicable authority. Project-facing communications remain with Laura/Ivan, including when financial advice is consulted internally.

Each row has one A. Where A also appears under R, that person owns and performs the work. Names under C do not create a mandatory approval chain. Teams receive information needed for their work, not automatically every sensitive document.

**Process ownership and individual case decisions are separate.** For example, Ivan monitors the refund queue, but any team member may decide and execute a routine refund: the case record names that person.

#### 3. Responsibility matrix

**Executive direction, team and governance**

| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 01  | Set strategy, priorities and overall capacity                                              | JF    | JF                                                                                                                                            | Laura, CFO                                            | Ivan, Board                                     |
| 02  | Prepare and submit a reserved decision                                                     | Board | JF                                                                                                                                            | CFO, Laura; competent adviser depending on the matter | People implementing the decision                |
| 03  | Decide recruitment, roles, remuneration and resource changes                               | JF    | JF                                                                                                                                            | Laura; CFO for the budget                             | People concerned                                |
| 04  | Allocate routine work and organise cover                                                   | Laura | Laura; each role holder for their handover                                                                                                    | Ivan, CFO; JF for capacity conflicts                  | Relevant team                                   |

**Agreed decision rules:**

* CFO is accountable for financial control but does not pre-approve every routine action. Collective approval and OCE checks remain necessary for payments.
* The entire team retains the refund authorisation given by JF. Row 28 does not give Ivan a veto over routine refunds.
* CFO remains the accounting coordination point. Laura and Ivan may participate in factual exchanges with Saïd; treatment instructions, accounting-period corrections and conclusions remain coordinated by CFO. This replaces the overly rigid ban on all direct contact in the previous matrix.
* Reconciliations have been deferred to **cycle 2**; this changes neither their owner nor the need to distinguish provisional from validated figures.
* Any independent review required by a funder is a separate engagement: it does not follow merely from CFO or Saïd appearing in the RACI.
